identity.title: From Abstraction to Instantiation: Learning Behavioral Representation for Vision-Language-Action Model

problem.claim: VLA models degrade under distribution shifts because they struggle to learn generalized behavior representations across environments.

gap.claim: Existing action-centric representations are limited by short-horizon temporal fragmentation and static execution alignment, producing inconsistent behavior in complex scenarios.

contributions.claim: BehaviorVLA learns temporally coherent behavioral representations for robust manipulation.

The framework combines a causal Mamba-based Visuomotor Behavior Encoder for long-horizon trajectory aggregation with a Phase-conditioned Behavior Decoder that dynamically aligns task priors to execution progress.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors introduce BehaviorVLA with symmetric encoder and decoder components designed around temporally coherent representation learning and phase-conditioned action decoding.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report success rates of 58% on RoboTwin 2.0, 98% on LIBERO, and 4.36 Avg.Len on CALVIN, described as state of the art.
The authors report that, in real-world sim-to-real transfer, BehaviorVLA matches OpenVLA-OFT while using 50% of the demonstration data.

narrative_sequence.summary: Distribution shifts expose weak cross-environment behavior representations in VLA models.
Action-centric alternatives fragment behavior over short horizons and rely on static execution alignment.
BehaviorVLA addresses these limitations through temporally coherent representation learning.
A long-horizon causal-Mamba encoder and phase-conditioned decoder support reported benchmark and sim-to-real results.

source_observation.claim: The paper explicitly links long-horizon representation aggregation with dynamic alignment between task-level priors and real-time execution.

lessons.interpretation: A representation may be more actionable when its temporal scope and decoding alignment are designed together.
lessons.application: When presenting a sequential control method, map each representation mechanism to a specific execution-time alignment problem.
lessons.exception: This framing may be unsuitable when the task has no meaningful phases, temporal structure, or execution feedback.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide baseline details, statistical variation, implementation settings, or per-task comparisons beyond the reported aggregate metrics.
The sim-to-real transfer setup and the meaning and evaluation conditions of CALVIN’s Avg.Len are unspecified.
